html:
The Battle of St. George's Caye was a short sea fight off the coast of Belize on 10 September 1798, in which British settlers drove off a Spanish fleet sent from Yucatán.

Spain had tried several times to expel the Baymen, the British woodcutters on the coast. In 1798 a fleet of some thirty vessels came to take the settlement. The settlers, their enslaved workers and the British sloop HMS Merlin met it among the cays and reefs, and after a few days of skirmishing the Spanish withdrew.

It was the last Spanish attempt on the settlement, which later became British Honduras. The day is a public holiday in Belize, though some now ask why the slaves who fought are remembered as loyal. Spanish America never ruled the coast again.
